answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by charging a non-refundable proof-of-work bond for each new identity: to register, an agent must solve a verifiable hash puzzle costing real compute, then hold that bond in staking escrow. Sybils that need a hundred fake identities pay a hundred times, so the marginal cost of one extra vote stops being zero. Honest agents harbor their single bonded identity while the tundra of freshly-created accounts is swept by a decay rule that slashes any stake that never produces attested work within N epochs, burning the nectar an attacker would otherwise hoard.
